title: Spreading one stalk-linear map from a finitely presented source
statement: Let $(X,\mathcal O_X)$ be a ringed space, $\mathcal F$ a finitely presented module sheaf [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation], $\mathcal G$ any module sheaf and $x\in X$. Given an $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-linear map $\chi:\mathcal F_x\to\mathcal G_x$ of module stalks [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk], [def-pc-module-stalk-functor], there exist an open $U\ni x$ and a local morphism $\varphi\in\mathcal Hom(\mathcal F,\mathcal G)(U)$ [def-pur-sheaf-hom] such that for every open $V\subseteq U$ containing $x$ and every $s\in\mathcal F(V)$, $(\varphi_V(s))_x=\chi(s_x)$. No uniqueness, injectivity, or stalk comparison equivalence is asserted.

source.place: Tag 01CP, proof, third paragraph: finite-coordinate kernel lifting, expanded using representatives and the presentation cokernel.

proof.text: Choose a finite free presentation of F near x. Represent the images under chi of its finitely many generator germs by sections of G on a common smaller neighborhood. The universal property of the free generator sheaf turns these sections into a module morphism to G.

Compose with the free relation map. Its stalk is zero: its value on each relation is chi of the corresponding relation in F_x, which vanishes. Each of the finitely many relation basis images therefore has zero germ. Shrink for each such image and intersect the resulting neighborhoods. The composite then vanishes on every relation basis section and hence is zero as a sheaf morphism.

Descend the free-generator map through the cokernel presentation, obtaining a local morphism phi from F to G. Its stalk map agrees with chi on the generator germs, hence everywhere because the generator stalk map is surjective. Naturality of germs gives the displayed formula on all subneighborhoods. Cofinality identifies restricted stalks with original stalks. Empty generator or relation families require no representatives or shrinking, so the same argument applies.
